title: Admin Impersonation Flow
purpose: Admin impersonation: start impersonation → X-Impersonating-User-Id header → protect middleware swap → impersonated request → ImpersonationBanner → stop impersonation.
audience: Engineers, security reviewers, admin panel developers
description: Complete admin impersonation lifecycle showing how an admin can act as any user. Start: admin navigates to user management, clicks 'Impersonate' on target user, saves impersonating_user_id to localStorage, navigates to hub/feed. Impersonated request: apiClient interceptor reads impersonating_user_id from storage and attaches X-Impersonating-User-Id header to every request. Protect middleware verifies admin JWT, detects header, confirms admin role, fetches target user profile, sets req.originalUser = admin and req.user = reshapedTargetUser. All downstream logic sees req.user as target user. UI shows ImpersonationBanner 'You are impersonating {name}'. Stop: admin clicks 'Stop Impersonating', clears localStorage, navigates to admin dashboard, subsequent requests return to normal admin auth. No server-side session tracking—purely client-driven via header.

decisions.falsePath: Continue normal authenticated request flow (no impersonation)

errorPaths.trigger: Impersonating user ID not found in DB
errorPaths.recovery: Admin must verify target user ID or check if user was deleted

errorPaths.destination: Impersonation header ignored—normal auth flow continues
errorPaths.recovery: No error—header silently discarded for non-admin users

errorPaths.trigger: Admin's own JWT expired during impersonation
errorPaths.recovery: Admin must re-authenticate and restart impersonation

validationRules: X-Impersonating-User-Id header is only honored for admin users
Target user must exist in profiles table
Impersonation does not bypass role guards—admin still has admin role in req.originalUser
businessRules: Impersonation is purely client-driven via header—no server-side session state
req.originalUser preserves admin identity for audit trail
ImpersonationBanner is essential UI feedback—without it admin may not realize they're impersonating
securityConsiderations: No server-side impersonation audit log exists
Impersonation does not require re-authentication or confirmation
Any component checking req.user gets impersonated identity—could lead to unintended actions
Purely client-driven: if admin shares their token, impersonation context is transferred
performanceConsiderations: Impersonation adds 1 extra DB query (fetch target user) per request
Total: 3 Supabase calls per impersonated request (getUser + admin fetch + target fetch)

annotations.text: Impersonation state stored in localStorage—persists across browser sessions
Only admin role can impersonate—enforced at middleware level
All services, models, and controllers see req.user as target user—no impersonation awareness downstream
